### [On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Sep/8/on-navier-stokes/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-09-08

OpenAI claims an unreleased model resolved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem using 130 billion tokens, sparking controversy over potential training data leaks from competing researchers.

- OpenAI used an internal agent system running for 88 hours that generated 2.7 million messages and 130 billion output tokens to solve the Navier-Stokes problem.
- Lean formalization and verification of the proof were completed in 17 hours using GPT-6 Astra.
- Across all tested Millennium Prize problems, OpenAI's agents consumed approximately 300 billion output tokens, an volume estimated at $15,000,000 at public API rates.
- NYU Professor Tristan Buckmaster accused OpenAI of potential data contamination after he and Anthropic employee Levent Alpöge used GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude to draft their own breakthrough prior to OpenAI's run.
- OpenAI denied accessing specific user data for the prompt, but acknowledged it could not rule out that de-identified user data from Codex sessions helped train their models.

**Why it matters:** This marks a major milestone in automated mathematics, while highlighting severe intellectual property and data-privacy tensions when researchers input unreleased scientific breakthroughs into commercial LLMs.

`ai` `openai` `mathematics` `navier-stokes` `llm`
